newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SOCCER-TEAR GAS INCIDENT DELAYS INDONESIAN SOCCER FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEAR GAS INCIDENT DELAYS INDONESIAN SOCCER FINAL.

text.p: Indonesian soccer officials have postponed Sunday's national league final by one day after several players were taken to hospital during a semifinal on Friday when tear gas drifted on to the pitch.

The official Antara news agency quoted Nugraha Besoes, secretary-general of the All Indonesia Soccer Association (PSSI), as saying that the last 28 minutes of the semifinal between Bandung Raya and Mitra Surabaya would be played on Saturday evening.
Another team, Persebaya Surabaya, has already won through to the final, which has been postponed from Sunday to Monday.
"If the final went ahead on Sunday as scheduled one of the finalists, either Bandung Raya or Mitra Surabaya, would not be in a fit condition as they would not have had a rest day," Besoes said.
Friday's semifinal was halted with Bandung leading 1-0. Newspapers said eight Surabaya players were taken to hospital after inhaling the gas, but said it was unclear who had fired the shells.
The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted police as denying any security officials had fired tear gas and were investigating.

Jakarta is regularly hit by crowd violence at the time of the national football finals and the U.S. embassy on Friday warned all citizens to stay away from the area surrounding the Senayan stadium in the city until the competition was over.

On Thursday, Jakarta police arrested more than 630 football fans from out of town after a wave of petty street crime which was blamed on the fact that many fans came to the capital to watch the games without sufficient money to support themselves.
